title: Nimman Chiang Mai 2026 — Cafes, One Nimman & Maya | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A walkable guide to Nimmanhaemin (Nimman) in Chiang Mai, Thailand: the best cafes, northern Thai food, shopping at One Nimman and Maya, and the night market — with real locations, rough prices, and how to see it all in a day.
keywords: Nimmanhaemin, Nimman Chiang Mai, One Nimman, Maya Chiang Mai, Nimman cafes
intro: Nimmanhaemin is where younger Chiang Mai locals actually hang out. Design-led cafes line up soi after soi, and a few steps in any direction get you to northern Thai restaurants, bars, a night market, and two big malls: One Nimman and Maya. We walked the whole area to figure out what's here, where to start, and how to fit it into a single day.

blocks.html: If Chiang Mai's Old City is the side with temples and history, Nimmanhaemin is the lifestyle side. The district sits just west of the moat, near Chiang Mai University. The spine is Nimmanhaemin Road, with numbered side streets (Soi 1 up to around Soi 17) branching off it. Each soi is packed with cafes, restaurants, handmade-goods shops, and places to stay, and because everything sits close together it's easy to explore on foot.

The charm of Nimman is how much variety fits into a small footprint. Morning coffee at a cafe, afternoon shopping for homeware, dinner of khao soi or northern Thai food, then a night market or a rooftop bar — all within walking distance. It suits anyone who doesn't want to drive far but still wants the buzz of a city that feels alive.

blocks.text: Where to start — a simple map of Nimman

items: Nimmanhaemin Road (the main strip) — the central axis of the district. Odd-numbered sois run off one side, even numbers off the other, with cafes and restaurants spread along them.
One Nimman — at the top of Nimman Road where it meets Huay Kaew Road. A Lanna-meets-European community mall with a clock tower as its landmark.
Maya Lifestyle Shopping Center (Maya) — a large mall on the Rin Kham intersection, directly across from One Nimman. You can walk between the two.
Think Park — a small community space next to Maya, with coffee shops and homeware stores that are nice for a wander.
Soi Wat Umong / the far end sois of Nimman — the quieter side, with garden cafes tucked away. Good for settling in for a while.

blocks.title: How to walk it without wearing yourself out
blocks.html: Park or get dropped near One Nimman or Maya (both have parking), then walk into the sois from there. Midday sun is strong, so start in the morning or late afternoon. At night the district is easy and safe to walk.

blocks.text: Nimman cafes that are still open and worth the talk

blocks.html: Nimman is the real cafe capital of Chiang Mai — everything from latte-art champions to quiet garden cafes. These are the spots we pulled from reviews that are still open and that people genuinely stop at (prices are rough ranges, and it's worth double-checking opening hours before you go).

items.name: Ristr8to
items.blurb: A serious latte-art coffee shop — the owner has won the World Latte Art championship. The signature is the Satan Latte with its copper swirl in the glass, and the coffee itself is genuinely strong, not just pretty. A pilgrimage stop for coffee people in Nimman.

items.name: Graph One Nimman
items.blurb: The branch inside the One Nimman community mall, with a dark, premium-feeling fit-out. The signature is a house blended coffee using beans from Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai farms. An easy place to sip while you shop.

items.name: % Arabica Chiang Mai (One Nimman)
items.blurb: The well-known Japanese coffee brand. The Chiang Mai branch sits in One Nimman with a clean white minimalist design and rich, aromatic coffee. There's usually a line of people photographing the % sign.

items.name: Ombra Caffè
items.blurb: A shady, leafy cafe on Soi 13 where you can sit quietly looking out at the trees and garden. There's coffee plus light bites, good for anyone who wants to escape the busier main road.

items.name: Ji Matcha Tea Time
items.blurb: A Japanese-style matcha cafe in One Nimman using quality green tea, with matcha lattes, mochi, cake, and ice cream. Quiet and comfortable to sit in, and a good pick if you don't drink coffee.

items.name: Hommwan Durian Cafe
items.blurb: A durian-focused cafe on Soi 5 with soft durian cake, durian ice cream, and durian drinks. A must for durian lovers, and there are other menu items if you're not into it.

items.name: Morestto
items.blurb: A heavily styled cafe on Soi 6 with photogenic corners everywhere — the stairs, the tables, the storefront. There's coffee and bakery to choose from, ideal for content creators after good shots.

items.name: Cypress Lane
items.blurb: An airy cafe looking out onto trees and greenery. Good for working or meeting a friend for a long chat — the main draw is the roomy, uncramped space.

blocks.title: Tips for cafe hopping
blocks.html: Many Nimman cafes close in the early evening (around 5–6pm), so if you want to hit several in one day, starting before noon gets you more. Popular spots get busy on weekends, so leave some buffer for a table.

The district's two main shopping spots have clearly different styles. For handmade goods, craft, and a photo-friendly atmosphere, go to One Nimman. For air-conditioning, brand-name stores, a supermarket, and a cinema, go to Maya. Both are a short walk across the road from each other.

items.name: One Nimman
items.blurb: A red-brick, Lanna-meets-European community mall with a clock tower as the check-in point. It gathers local brands, craft, design-led souvenirs, cafes, bars, and northern Thai restaurants. Open roughly 11am–10pm daily.

items.name: Maya Lifestyle (Maya)
items.blurb: A 6-floor mall plus rooftop, with a Rimping supermarket in the basement, a northern Thai food court on level 4, an SFX cinema on level 5, and a rooftop with Doi Suthep views. Open roughly 10am–10pm daily.

items.name: Think Park
items.blurb: A small community space next to Maya with coffee shops, homeware stores, and outdoor seating. Good for a quick stop before or after the mall.

blocks.html: At Maya, the spot people love is the top-floor rooftop with views over the city and Doi Suthep — especially nice at sunset, with bars and seating for a drink. The basement has Rimping, a supermarket Chiang Mai locals favor, which is great for premium snacks and edible souvenirs.

Nimman isn't only cafes — the food is serious too, from northern Thai dishes to international restaurants to street food in the night market. Prices run from a few dozen baht a plate up to sit-down restaurants.

items: Maha Larb CNZ (One Nimman) — northern Thai food done tapas-style on small plates, many dishes around THB 30–70. Order several to share for a spread of northern flavors in one meal.

Khao soi & northern Thai food — there are khao soi and northern Thai restaurants scattered across several sois around Nimman. Most open from morning to afternoon, so going before noon is the safer bet.
Maya food court (level 4) — Thai and northern dishes at easy prices, in the low tens of baht per plate. Good for a quick meal on a hot day.
International restaurants in Nimman — Italian, Japanese, and Korean spread across the sois, ideal if you've had enough Thai food and want a change.

blocks.html: Once the sun drops, Nimman shifts into evening-meetup mode. The spot people head to is the night market at One Nimman, around the clock-tower plaza (One Square), with around 20–30 street-food stalls of both northern Thai and Western fare like gelato, barbecue chicken, and pork ribs. It runs Friday–Sunday only, roughly 3–10pm, and at times there's live music and art to round out the mood.

blocks.title: Planning around the market
blocks.html: The One Nimman night market only runs Friday–Sunday. If you come on a weekday and still want a night market, try the Sunday Walking Street in the Old City instead, or one of the other night markets around town.

blocks.text: Nimman in one day — a real walking plan

blocks.html: If you've got a single day and want to cover Nimman's cafes, shopping, and food, here's an order that walks comfortably without doubling back. Adjust it to your own pace.

items.note: Go early to dodge the crowds and get a comfy seat

items.activity: Walk the Nimman sois, stopping at handmade-goods shops and photo cafes
items.note: Sois 5–13 have plenty worth a stop

items.activity: Lunch of northern Thai food, or Maha Larb in One Nimman
items.note: Order several small plates to share

items.activity: Shop One Nimman for craft souvenirs and photograph the clock tower
items.note: There are cafes inside for a break

items.activity: Cross to Maya, browse the mall out of the sun, stop by Rimping in the basement
items.note: Pick up snacks and premium souvenirs here

items.activity: Head up to the Maya rooftop for sunset over Doi Suthep
items.note: The evening air is just right

items.activity: One Nimman night market at the clock-tower plaza (Fri–Sun)
items.note: On weekdays, hit a restaurant or bar in the sois instead

items.note: It's a safe walk back to your hotel from here

items: From the Old City — about 2–3 km away. Take a red truck (songthaew) or grab a Grab/Bolt — both easy, and the fare isn't expensive.
Red truck (songthaew) — you can flag one anywhere in town; agree the price before getting in, starting from the low tens of baht per person.
Rent a motorbike/car — Nimman has parking at One Nimman and Maya, but traffic backs up in the evening, so allow extra time.
Walk — once you're in the district everything's walkable, no need for a car between stops.

faq.q: Where is Nimmanhaemin (Nimman) in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: It's west of the old moat, near Chiang Mai University, about 2–3 km from the Old City. A red truck or a Grab gets you there in a few minutes. The main axis is Nimmanhaemin Road, with numbered side streets branching off it.

faq.q: How are One Nimman and Maya different — which should I go to?
faq.a: One Nimman is an open-air, Lanna-meets-European community mall focused on craft, design-led souvenirs, cafes, and the night market — good for photos and an easy stroll. Maya is an enclosed, air-conditioned 6-floor mall with brand stores, the Rimping supermarket, a cinema, and a rooftop with Doi Suthep views. The two face each other and you can walk across between them.

faq.q: What days is the One Nimman night market open?
faq.a: Friday through Sunday only, roughly 3–10pm, at the clock-tower plaza (One Square), with around 20–30 street-food stalls. If you come on a weekday, head to a restaurant in the sois or the Old City Walking Street instead.

faq.q: Which Nimman cafes are worth visiting?
faq.a: For specialty coffee, try Ristr8to on Soi 3, where the owner has won a world latte-art championship. For photos, try % Arabica and Graph in One Nimman. If you like a quiet garden vibe, try Ombra Caffè on Soi 13. Many close in the early evening, so start before noon.

faq.q: How long do I need for Nimman?
faq.a: If you walk the cafes, shop One Nimman and Maya, and have dinner, half a day to a full day is about right. The spots all sit close together and are walkable, so you won't need a car between them.
